notes: Cohere's own Rerank documentation. States "Rerank models sort text inputs by semantic relevance to a specified query. They are often used to sort search results returned from an existing search solution" — the distinct reranking function, separate from the generative Command family. The model table lists rerank-v3.5 with the note "This model has a context length of 4096 tokens" (the recorded contextWindow), and the only endpoint shown is POST https://api.cohere.com/v2/rerank requiring a bearer token, which is the API-only, proprietary-hosted access recorded. On lifecycle: Cohere's model overview (https://docs.cohere.com/docs/models) publishes a Status column for the Command table (values "Live" and "Deprecated Sept 15, 2025") and for Parse, but the Rerank table has no Status column and this Rerank page states no lifecycle term, so no source states whether rerank-v3.5 is current — the basis for status unknown under ADR 0008. On the family's first release: this page states no origin date for Rerank at any precision, and the abdeslam-menacere/ModelTree#740 investigation found no Cohere source that states one. Three candidates were reviewed there and each rejected: 2024-12-02, which is rerank-v3.5's own release date rather than the family's first; 2024-04-09, which is Rerank 3's date, and Cohere's own deprecations page shows a generation predates it by announcing "On December 2nd, 2024, we announced the release of Rerank-v3.5 along with the deprecation of the Rerank-v2.0 model family"; and 2023-05-01, a JSON-LD datePublished on https://cohere.com/blog/rerank, whose body is JS-rendered and whose earliest Wayback snapshot is 2024-04-19, so it could not be corroborated. Absence rather than imprecision is the point -- partialDate already expresses a year-only date -- and it is the basis for datePrecision unstated under ADR 0013. Cited for the family's reranking function, the API-only access, the 4096-token context length, the unknown lifecycle status, and the unstated first release date.
